description:
`_agent_verify_final` runs the project's verify hook inside a COMMAND SUBSTITUTION and under the wrong phase, so a legitimately long final verify is indistinguishable from a hang. Measured on talos, 2026-09-03.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. `talos:83-slice-lane-execution` ran 7h41m and read `⚠ stalled in agent-turn — no activity for 1h06m, past its 15m limit`. The branch was HEALTHY: 7 commits, 58 files, 2,752 insertions, 4/4 stories passing, `stall: 0`. The agent emitted `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` at log line 192 and the log ENDS THERE — 192 of 192 lines. It did not hang working; it hung finishing, invisibly.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE — the first half:

    output="$(run_verify "$CHIEF_PROJECT" "$CHIEF_TASKLIST" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
    printf '%s\n' "$output"

Command substitution. Nothing reaches the log until the verify RETURNS. And `_beat_start` flips the phase to `writing` only when `_head` moves — so with the output captured, nothing moves, the record stops advancing, and the monitor has no signal but silence.

WHY IT FLAGGED AT 15 MINUTES — the second half, and this one is nearly free. `monitor.sh`'s `STALE_PHASE_SECONDS` already gives `verifying` **3060s** against `provider-waiting`'s 900s, precisely because a verify legitimately takes tens of minutes. But `grep -n 'phase=verifying' engine/` returns exactly ONE call site — `driver.sh:2928`. `_agent_verify_final` never publishes it, so its verify is timed as an agent turn. The right threshold exists and this code path does not use it.

WHAT MADE IT LONG RATHER THAN WEDGED. `83`'s diff touched 17 files under `talos/slices/` and `vendor/insimul/`, which arms the gate whose own comment states the cost: 'one Godot launch and one editor'. `test_godot_slice_driver.py` launches a real Godot process three times through `BridgeLauncher`; `test_unity_slice_driver.py` drives a `UnityEditor`. That is minutes at best and can block. The verify was probably doing its job — nobody could tell.

RELATED AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `117` stopped `_agent_verify_final` re-running a verify whose verdict is already recorded. It did nothing about the case where the verify legitimately runs, which is this one. `117` also was not INSTALLED on the machine that produced this — `~/.chief/src` was 0.9.8 against a repo at 0.9.10 — so the run paid the duplication too. That is an operator gap, not a code gap, and this tasklist does not try to fix it.

THE MONITOR'S OWN RULE IS THE SPEC. `live.sh`: 'a wait must never render as work or as a hang.' `monitor.sh` on the provider-waiting threshold: '15m of silence in this phase is ~60 missed beats: the turn is not long, the ticker is DEAD.' Both are right, and both were defeated by a code path that goes quiet on purpose.

userStories.title: The final verify streams, so the record keeps moving
acceptanceCriteria: `_agent_verify_final` streams the verify hook's output to the log as it is produced rather than capturing it in a command substitution. The exit status must still be the hook's — a pipeline that returns the wrong status here would let a red verify accept a completion, which is worse than the bug being fixed.
The verdict is still recorded through `verify_cache_record` exactly as now, and a failure still sets `COMPLETE_OK=0`. This story changes when bytes appear, not what the gate decides.

A test asserts output appears BEFORE the hook exits — drive a hook that prints, sleeps, then prints, and assert the first line is observable while it still runs. Asserting only on the final log contents cannot tell streaming from buffering.
GATES: `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S error`, the behavioral tests, doc-sync, and the VERSION bump the engine-change gate requires.

userStories.title: It publishes the phase whose threshold already fits it
acceptanceCriteria: `_agent_verify_final` publishes `phase=verifying` for the duration of the hook and restores the prior phase afterwards. The threshold it needs already exists in `STALE_PHASE_SECONDS` at 3060s and had exactly one publisher; this adds the second.

The heartbeat keeps ticking across the verify, and `_beat_start` does NOT clobber `verifying` with `writing` when output moves. Streaming output would otherwise re-label a verify as writing on its first line, which trades one wrong phase for another.

`chief ps` on a running final verify reads as verifying with a live tick — not as a stalled agent turn. State what it renders; a phase nobody can see in the monitor has not been published where it matters.

userStories.title: The stall flag still fires on a real hang
acceptanceCriteria: A NEGATIVE CONTROL: a hook that produces no output and never exits must STILL be reported stale once `verifying`'s threshold passes. The fix must not buy quiet by exempting the phase — `monitor.sh` refuses that trade explicitly for provider-waiting ('It wants a LONGER threshold, not silence'), and the same reasoning binds here.

A test distinguishes the two cases the incident conflated: a long verify that is emitting (not stale) and a dead verify that is not (stale). Both assertions, or the change has moved the problem rather than fixed it.
`docs/guides/monitoring.md`'s phase table records that `verifying` now has two publishers and what a reader should conclude from it, since that table is what an operator consults at 1am.
